changelog: Added Dioralyte 8 sachets/L and Clinova 16 tablets/L specialist regimens, dual sourced St Mark’s citrate options, a glucose-only Pocari Sweat-style home recreation, shareable URL state, print layout, composition profiles and explicit osmotic provenance.

recipes.name: St Mark’s solution
recipes.method: Dissolve the weighed ingredients in the displayed volume of cold drinking water. The source specifies water added, not a measured final volume.
recipes.storage: Prepare fresh each day. Discard after 24 hours.
recipes.basis: Calculated assuming pure anhydrous glucose and the exact salts shown. The source specifies ingredients added to 1 L water, so powder displacement is not modelled. The 285 mOsm/kg value is BIFA’s reported osmolality for the bicarbonate formulation.
recipes.warning: Use the formulation and volume advised by your clinical team. Table sugar and LoSalt are not substitutes in this potassium-free recipe.

sources.title: BIFA/BAPEN · ORS for high-output stomas and fistulas · May 2025

recipes.name: WHO ORS
recipes.method: Use the exact ingredient forms shown. Dissolve in drinking water and make up to the displayed final volume.
recipes.storage: Prepare fresh and use within 24 hours.
recipes.basis: Calculated from WHO ingredient masses. Rounded WHO targets: Na 75, K 20, Cl 65, glucose 75 and citrate 10 mmol/L; osmolarity 245 mOsm/L. Small differences reflect rounding.
recipes.warning: This is the current reduced-osmolarity WHO formulation, not the older 90 mmol/L sodium recipe. It contains potassium.

bicarb.label: Sodium bicarbonate · 2.5 g/L
bicarb.note: WHO-listed immediate-use substitution; bicarbonate/glucose dry mixtures are less stable in heat and humidity.

recipes.name: Dioralyte
recipes.method: Reference masses scale the product specification of one sachet per 200 mL water. They are not a validated home-compounding method. For the licensed product follow the sachet instructions.
recipes.storage: Licensed product: use promptly; discard after 1 hour at room temperature or 24 hours refrigerated. This does not validate storage of a homemade copy.
recipes.basis: Composition shown is the published commercial-product reference, not a calculated guarantee for these raw powders. The SmPC does not resolve glucose/citrate hydration forms. Excipients are excluded.
recipes.warning: Reference only: a homemade copy has not been shown equivalent to Dioralyte. Generic sodium citrate cannot replace disodium hydrogen citrate.

recipes.name: Dioralyte · 8 sachets/L
recipes.description: Specialist high-output regimen · eight sachets per litre
recipes.method: Specialist product regimen: dissolve 8 whole Dioralyte sachets in 1 litre of water (1 sachet per 125 mL). Listed raw ingredient masses are product-specification references, not a validated home copy.
recipes.storage: Prepare fresh each day and follow the storage instructions supplied by your clinical team.
recipes.basis: Eight times the licensed sachet composition in 1 L water. Electrolyte and glucose values are scaled from the published standard product. The osmolarity is a proportional estimate, not a measured value.
recipes.warning: This intentionally uses a stronger dilution than the licensed pack instructions. It contains approximately 32 mmol/L potassium.

recipes.name: Dioralyte double-strength
recipes.method: Specialist product regimen: 10 whole sachets in 1 litre of water (1 sachet per 100 mL). Do not split dry sachets. Listed raw ingredient masses are a reference, not a validated copy.
recipes.storage: Use your clinical team’s preparation and storage instructions.
recipes.basis: Twice the published standard-strength commercial composition. Osmolarity is a nominal doubled estimate, not a measured value. Raw-powder hydration forms and excipients remain unresolved.
recipes.warning: Double strength is off-label specialist use. Contains 40 mmol/L potassium; use only on specific clinical advice, with appropriate monitoring.

sources.title: BIFA/BAPEN · ORS for high-output stomas and fistulas · May 2025

recipes.name: Dioralyte Relief
recipes.method: Commercial product: mix one whole sachet with 200 mL drinking water until milky. Scaled raw masses are composition references, not a verified home recipe.
recipes.storage: Use within 1 hour, or within 24 hours if refrigerated.
recipes.basis: SmPC: each sachet contains 6 g pre-cooked rice, 580 mg sodium citrate, 350 mg sodium chloride and 300 mg potassium chloride. Displayed electrolyte and osmolarity values are the product’s published profile. Rice contributes starch and protein; its free glucose and polymer distribution are not specified.
recipes.warning: Relief is a separate rice-based formula, not standard Dioralyte with starch added. Raw powder copies and substitutions are unvalidated.

recipes.name: Pedialyte · unflavoured
recipes.description: US oral electrolyte solution · 59 mL presentation
recipes.method: Measure the displayed volume of the ready-to-use product. Do not add water. Individual salt masses are not disclosed, so a home-copy recipe cannot be established from this label.
recipes.storage: For this 59 mL presentation, discard after use; follow the package instructions.
recipes.basis: Abbott US unflavoured 59 mL label: sodium 2.8 mEq, potassium 1.2 mEq, chloride 2.1 mEq, zinc 0.50 mg and carbohydrate 1.2 g. Values are scaled to one litre; monovalent mEq equals mmol. Dextrose is listed as 1 g per bottle without a hydration basis; glucose mmol/L, citrate and numerical osmolarity are not established here.
recipes.warning: Product reference, not a homemade recipe. Other Pedialyte products and regional versions differ; check the exact label.

sources.title: Abbott · Pedialyte oral electrolyte solution (US 59 mL)

recipes.name: Clinova O.R.S · 16 tablets/L
recipes.description: Specialist high-output regimen · sixteen tablets per litre
recipes.method: Dissolve 16 whole Clinova O.R.S hydration tablets in 1 litre of tap water.
recipes.storage: Prepare a fresh solution each day.
recipes.basis: BIFA publishes the approximate composition of the 16-tablet regimen as sodium 96, potassium 40 and glucose 146 mmol/L. Individual ion and osmotic values not stated by that source remain blank.
recipes.warning: This is the specialist 16-tablet-per-litre regimen described by BIFA and Guy’s and St Thomas’, not the manufacturer’s ordinary hydration dilution.

recipes.name: Pocari Sweat-style · glucose recipe
recipes.description: Home recreation · label electrolyte targets with glucose only
recipes.method: Weigh the exact chemical forms shown and dissolve them in the displayed volume of drinking water. This reconstruction uses glucose as the only carbohydrate.
recipes.storage: Prepare fresh. Storage stability and microbiological shelf life have not been established for this home reconstruction.
recipes.basis: The electrolyte masses solve the Japanese powder label targets: Na 21, K 5, Cl 16, Ca 0.5, Mg 0.25, citrate 3.333 and lactate 1 mmol/L. Sodium chloride supplies 11 mmol sodium/chloride; potassium chloride supplies 5 mmol potassium/chloride; trisodium citrate dihydrate supplies 10 mmol sodium and 3.333 mmol citrate; calcium lactate pentahydrate supplies 0.5 mmol calcium and 1 mmol lactate. Glucose is set to the label’s 65 g/L total carbohydrate, so this is not osmotically or organoleptically equivalent to the mixed-sugar commercial powder.
recipes.warning: This is a transparent home reconstruction of the published electrolyte targets, not the commercial product. Exact salt hydration forms matter; 21 mg magnesium carbonate per litre requires a suitable milligram scale.

sources.title: Otsuka · Pocari Sweat, Japanese 1 L powder
